subject: Bolivia
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Bolivia and the War of the Pacific. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). Bolivia’s former coast is shown as a labelled point (approximate), not drawn from historical borders.

claims.text: During the War of the Pacific (1879–84), Chile occupied vast territories rich in natural resources southwest of Bolivia, including the Bolivian coast.
Chile took control of the Chuquicamata area, the adjoining saltpeter fields, and the port of Antofagasta among other Bolivian territories.
Bolivia lost its Litoral Department, and thus access to a maritime coast, following the War of the Pacific in 1883.
Bolivia has historically upheld a state policy asserting a maritime claim over the lost territory.

antofagasta.note: Antofagasta, the port town Chile took.
